storyPrompt: Write a quiet English story about checking a disputed delivery before a public demonstration. Nadi is a practical conservator. Wren is an assistant who is allowed to disagree. Sol keeps the public records. The story takes place at the kite hall. The wooden sleeve must remain intact. No character may be physically injured. Keep practical actions precise. Use third-person past tense centred on Nadi. Plan six chapters, each targeting 750 words. No earlier book or borrowed fictional world is assumed.

chapters.turn: Sol supplies a duplicate page; the team agrees to continue checking before a demonstration.

chapters.purpose: Nadi compares the duplicate with a pencil copy.
chapters.turn: Wren identifies a transposed line and they agree on a corrected label.

chapters.title: Demonstration
chapters.purpose: The team prepares the public demonstration at the kite hall.
chapters.turn: Nadi credits Wren for finding the error, without claiming the item was lost.

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.purpose: Nadi completes the demonstration and files the corrected flight register.
chapters.turn: The intact wooden sleeve is stored securely and the dispute is closed.

texts:
Nadi received the sealed wooden sleeve and checked its outer label. The kite hall was open, though there were no visitors at the table. Nadi cleared a space before setting anything down. Wren moved the loose tools to a tray and waited for instructions. Neither of them treated a late delivery as proof of a lost object. They checked what they could see and left a blank beside what they could not yet establish.

The work required a little patience. A faded number was difficult to distinguish from a stain, so Nadi turned the sheet towards the window rather than writing over it. Wren read the number aloud. They compared their readings, found that they agreed, and entered it only once. The wooden sleeve remained intact on the cleared table throughout the check.

Nadi made a short note of the work completed that day. The note separated observation from intention: a task written for tomorrow did not become a task already done. Wren asked whether the uncertainty meant they should abandon the demonstration. Nadi said that an unanswered question was a reason to check, rather than a reason to invent an answer. It was an ordinary distinction, but making it aloud helped them continue without blaming anyone.

Nadi noticed a red seam but left it unopened. They put the tools back in the tray. Nadi recorded that result and closed the current work period. The next planned task remained unwritten in the story. No one had opened a different room, visited another site, or completed the later demonstration in the interval between these actions.
